claims: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket lifted off.
The SLS rocket sent astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen on a 10-day journey around the Moon.
Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
The crew is safely in orbit.
There was a minor reported issue with the Orion capsule's toilet system.
The 10-day mission is the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
The mission is testing critical systems for future lunar landings.
The SLS rocket produced 8.8 million pounds of force.
The launch had a 90% "go" rating for favorable weather.
The crew includes NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman (commander).
The crew includes NASA astronaut Victor Glover (pilot).
The crew includes NASA astronaut Christina Koch (mission specialist).
The crew includes CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist).
The mission successfully began the next phase of the Artemis program.
